title: JavaScript
subtitle: The language of the web, from a first script to asynchronous programs, browser code and the tools professionals use every day.
description: JavaScript is the programming language built into every web browser, and with Node.js, Deno and Bun it also runs web servers, command-line tools, build systems and desktop apps. It first appeared in 1995 and is standardised as ECMAScript by Ecma International's TC39 committee, which publishes a new edition every year. This course teaches modern JavaScript as of ECMAScript 2025: values and types (and the coercions that trip people up), control flow and functions, closures and `this`, objects, prototypes and classes, arrays and collections, errors and testing, the event loop and async/await, the browser's DOM and events, and the tools of a working JavaScript developer, ending with a complete small project.

It is written for anyone who has finished the Start level of [Lumenary CS](/en/cs/), or has equivalent experience: you know what a variable, a loop and a function are, in any language. No experience of the web is assumed.

To run the examples, install the current long-term-support (LTS) release of Node.js from [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/en/download), save a program as `main.mjs` and run `node main.mjs`. Every complete program in these lessons is run by Lumenary's test suite as an ES module under Node 22, and the output shown beside it is what it actually printed. Code that needs a web page is shown separately and explained; you can try it in the developer console of any browser (open it with F12, or Cmd+Option+J on a Mac), which is the nearest thing JavaScript has to an official playground.
